initiatives.title: Locum Invoice Crossover & Payment Date
initiatives.why: Emily clarified that the calculation components are not complex. The real constraint is lab-invoice crossover: lab cost is not final at PO because rebates and credits are only recognised on the invoice, and the latest invoice can arrive about 10 days after PO. Tail-end invoices that miss cutoff are currently deducted in the following month. The risk is assigning every invoice once, to the right doctor and source month, at the source month's effective locum rate.
initiatives.next: Recommended: keep the current payment date, add a formal carry-forward ledger that preserves each invoice's source month and rate, and shrink the invoice tail by agreeing an invoicing cycle with the labs.
initiatives.gate: Any cutoff date has a tail — moving the date moves the boundary, it does not remove it. So fix the mechanics, not the date: stamp every late invoice with the month it belongs to and deduct it at that month's rate.
initiatives.timeline: Measure three closes → compare the three methods → decide the convention and payment date → document it.

tasks.t: Emily clarification: the formula is simple; invoice timing and month crossover are the real constraint
Finding: rebates and credits are only final on invoice; the latest invoice may arrive about 10 days after PO
Log PO→invoice timing, rebates and every late-invoice carry-forward for three closes
Model Option 1 — pay on the 15th and eliminate routine monthly contra/carry-forward
Model Option 2 — one-month lab lag, preserving each source month's production threshold and effective rate
Model Option 3 — current cutoff with a formal digital carry-forward ledger
Issue a per-doctor statement with every payment — do this now, regardless of the date
Choose the calculation convention and payment date, then write both into the agreement
Deduct carried-forward invoices at their SOURCE month's rate — the current method quietly applies the wrong one
Agree a fixed invoicing cycle with the labs to shrink the tail

initiatives.note: Digital calculation can reduce Emily's work, but it does not by itself solve invoice crossover. A one-month lag is only safe if late deductions retain the originating month's rate; otherwise the RM55k whole-month volume rule can price the cost incorrectly.

initiatives.title: Invisalign Invoice Verification — off the doctor
initiatives.why: A doctor personally checks every aligner invoice to make sure we were billed correctly. The right question is what she is checking it against — and the answer exposes the design flaw: she is reconstructing the truth at month end from knowledge only she holds. Verification belongs with the office, in line with the direction that all supplier communication and invoicing sits with management. The office already has portal access; the obstacle is that the account is segregated by invoice rather than by patient name, so an invoice line cannot be traced back to a case without the doctor's knowledge.
initiatives.next: Access is not the blocker — the office already has it. The account is organised by invoice rather than by patient, so the real task is defining what has to be captured for an invoice to be checkable without the doctor.
initiatives.gate: Capture the truth when it is created, not months later. The doctor confirms the case at the moment it is ordered — thirty seconds — and the office verifies the invoice against that log with no doctor involved.
initiatives.timeline: Access and price list Aug → case log running Sep → first office-run verification Oct. Automated matching later.

tasks.t: Office portal access — already in place
Define exactly what is needed to tie an invoice line to a case, given the account is invoice-segregated not patient-segregated
Obtain the current price list and volume-tier agreement
Start the case log — case ID, patient, doctor, product, date, refinements
First month verified by the office, checked alongside the doctor
Automated invoice-to-case matching to flag discrepancies

initiatives.note: Volume-tier pricing on aligners is a cost-line rebate under the rebates policy.

initiatives.title: AI Clinical Note Transcription
initiatives.why: Doctors spend real chair time typing the patient conversation into notes. That time is the most expensive time in the building, and the task is now genuinely easy to automate: record the conversation, transcribe it, and format it into the clinic's own note style.
initiatives.next: Hold until the clinician comes back with what she actually wants. The note data showed she is third by volume, so the problem may not be the one we assumed.
initiatives.gate: Two non-negotiables: patient consent for recording, and the doctor reviews and approves before anything enters the clinical record. Never auto-write.
initiatives.blockedOn: Waiting on the clinician to define what she means by transcription.
initiatives.timeline: Short term: a handheld device in the room. Medium term: a fixed microphone per surgery, with patients matched by timestamp against the appointment book.

tasks.t: Get the clinical definition of the problem before building anything
Collect sample notes to learn the output format
Recording consent — folded into the onboarding form redesign
Prototype: recording → transcription → formatted note
Trial in one surgery with doctor review before saving
Fixed microphone per room, matched to the appointment book by timestamp

initiatives.note: Run the model locally so no patient audio or clinical text leaves the premises — the privacy-safe answer and the easiest one to defend to the doctors.

initiatives.title: Patient Conversation Context for Doctors
initiatives.why: When a patient arrives having asked something technical by message beforehand, the doctor needs that context. The agreed short-term fix is to put the messaging app on a surgery computer for the upstairs doctors — recorded here so it gets re-examined rather than quietly becoming permanent.
initiatives.next: Confirm the placement, then decide whether the shared computer is the right long-term answer or an interim.
initiatives.gate: The messaging app is a channel; the patient record is the system of record. Context should reach the doctor where they already look.
initiatives.timeline: Interim placement now. Target state — front desk logs the substance onto the appointment note — lands with the front-of-house SOP.

tasks.t: Confirm placement — the lab space opposite the rooms on each floor, so no doctor is advantaged or disadvantaged
Check the linked-device limit — it cannot go on every doctor's machine
Front desk logs the substance of message exchanges onto the appointment note
Review after a month: is the shared computer still needed?

initiatives.note: A shared computer is a workaround. The real fix is the front-of-house SOP, which puts the context into the record.

initiatives.title: DSA Training Programme
initiatives.why: There is no structured training for the dental surgery assistants. The doctors already run a quarterly get-together where they teach each other what they have learned — the same model would work chairside, and running it is a real ownership opportunity for the senior assistants rather than a chore.
initiatives.next: Confirm who runs it, then draft the competency matrix and the first session.
initiatives.gate: A competency matrix per assistant, a quarterly session, and a sign-off — so it feeds the staff scorecard rather than being a one-off.
initiatives.timeline: Design Aug–Sep → first session Q4 2026 → quarterly thereafter.

tasks.t: Confirm who leads it
Draft the competency matrix
Design the first session
Run the first quarterly session
Fold competencies into the staff scorecard

initiatives.note: The hybrid front-desk / chairside staff should have their chairside and front-desk competencies on one sheet.

initiatives.title: New Doctor — capacity & case-mix hire
initiatives.why: Our own margin data shows a very wide spread in value produced per chair-hour between doctors — one clinician generates several hundred times the true margin per hour of another. Business as usual will not close the gap in time. A clinician who can arrive and immediately deliver higher-value procedures, and bring patients with them, is the case-mix lever — the only route past the capacity ceiling other than extending hours.
initiatives.next: A first conversation is happening now. The founders are aligned that this needs to happen. The work to get right is how it is explained to the doctors already here.
initiatives.gate: Plan the message to the existing practitioners before anything becomes public. A new practitioner means competition for chair time and patients, and that is the part most likely to go wrong.
initiatives.timeline: Prior conversations already held — this is a re-open, not a cold approach. Terms would ride on the contractor agreement.

tasks.t: First conversation held
Agree what a strong first year looks like, in chair-hours and case mix
Terms via the contractor agreement
Agree how this is communicated to the practitioners already here

initiatives.note: Sits alongside the specialist-surgeon conversation already on the board — both are the same lever.

initiatives.title: Recall Campaign Expansion — cold blast & post-visit follow-up
initiatives.why: The recall system was built with more triggers than the six, nine and twelve-month recalls we actually switched on. Turning the others on is the cheapest top-line lever available, and the P&L trajectory says business as usual will not close the gap. Messaging even ten thousand lapsed patients costs on the order of RM3,000.
initiatives.next: Decision taken: send from the landline. Brief the vendor, then ship the review ask — it needs only a direct review link and no redirect.
initiatives.gate: Do not launch anything while the recall link is broken — blasting the whole base into a browser security warning is worse than not blasting at all.
initiatives.timeline: UNBLOCKED 18 Jul — the recall link certificate is renewed (valid to 16 Oct) and the vendor has automated the renewal. Post-visit follow-up amendment first (fast, free), then the cold blast.

tasks.t: Decision taken — send from the landline now; stop waiting on the mobile approval
Brief the vendor to send the post-appointment message from the landline
Vendor renewed the expired certificate on the recall link — 18 Jul, valid to 16 Oct
Amend the post-appointment follow-up to also ask for a Google review — no reward, just that it helps others find us
Draft the cold reactivation blast, with a bring-the-family angle
De-conflict against the reactivation call lists so nobody gets both
Send, then measure honestly — correlation is not proven lift
Birthday messages — de-prioritised
Certificate auto-renewal automated by the vendor (cron added, confirmed 21 Jul)

initiatives.note: Birthday trigger de-prioritised by the owner. The review ask moves a lever that already feeds the website automatically.
